data.title: QR Code Payment Fraud (Quishing) — Malicious QR Destination to Credential Harvesting Infrastructure
data.description: Detects quishing attacks by identifying emails or messages containing QR code images where the encoded URL resolves to a recently registered domain (under 30 days), a known URL shortener redirecting to a credential harvesting page, or a domain impersonating postal services or banking institutions. INTERPOL's 2026 Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment documents a European modus operandi where fraudsters send fake QR codes claiming payment is available at a post office, routing victims through a fake postal site to a cloned bank login page. In a documented case, USD 110,000 was stolen through this method. The attack exploits a fundamental QR code UX gap: unlike hyperlinks, QR codes do not display a destination URL before the victim commits to following them. The subsequent 2FA device enrollment step converts credential capture into persistent account takeover, making real-time detection at the email/content analysis layer critical before the victim scans.

detection.condition: selection_qr_in_message AND (filter_new_domain OR filter_shortener_redirect OR filter_brand_impersonation)

enrichment_required.source: QR code detection via image analysis on email attachments and inline images
Decoded URL from QR code image content
Domain age lookup from WHOIS/domain intelligence feed for the decoded QR destination
Boolean flag indicating QR URL uses a known URL shortener service (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.)
Domain age of the final destination after following shortener redirects
Brand impersonation classification from domain intelligence (postal service, banking keywords)

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for QR Code Payment Fraud (Quishing) Detection
// Detects emails with QR codes pointing to new domains or credential harvesting infrastructure
attachment_contains_qr_code=true
| (qr_destination_domain_age_days<=30
   OR (qr_destination_is_shortener=true AND redirect_final_domain_age_days<=30)
   OR (qr_destination_domain_impersonates IN ["postal_service", "banking_institution"]
       AND qr_destination_domain_is_legitimate=false))
| groupBy(qr_destination_fqdn, span=24h, function=[
    count(distinct=recipient_email, as=distinct_recipients),
    count(message_id, as=message_count),
    collect([sender_email, subject, qr_destination_url, qr_destination_domain_age_days])
  ])
| sort(distinct_recipients, order=desc)
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for QR Code Payment Fraud (Quishing) Detection")`
`comment("Detects emails with QR codes resolving to new/suspicious domains")`
index=flame_email sourcetype=flame:content_analysis
  attachment_contains_qr_code="true"
| lookup domain_age_feed qr_destination_fqdn AS fqdn OUTPUT domain_age_days
| lookup url_shortener_list qr_destination_fqdn AS fqdn OUTPUT is_shortener
| lookup domain_age_feed redirect_final_fqdn AS fqdn OUTPUT domain_age_days AS redirect_domain_age
| eval is_new_domain = if(domain_age_days < 30, 1, 0)
| eval is_shortener_to_new = if(is_shortener="true" AND redirect_domain_age < 30, 1, 0)
| eval is_brand_impersonation = if(
    match(qr_destination_fqdn, "(?i)(post|mail|parcel|bank|login|secure|verify)")
    AND qr_destination_domain_is_legitimate="false", 1, 0)
| where is_new_domain=1 OR is_shortener_to_new=1 OR is_brand_impersonation=1
| eval detection_reason = case(
    is_brand_impersonation=1, "brand_impersonation",
    is_shortener_to_new=1, "shortener_redirect_to_new_domain",
    is_new_domain=1, "new_domain")
| eval risk_level = case(
    is_brand_impersonation=1 AND domain_age_days < 7, "critical",
    is_brand_impersonation=1, "high",
    is_shortener_to_new=1, "high",
    1=1, "medium")
| stats dc(recipient_email) AS distinct_recipients, count AS message_count,
    values(sender_email) AS senders, values(subject) AS subjects,
    values(qr_destination_url) AS qr_urls, values(detection_reason) AS detection_reasons
    by qr_destination_fqdn, risk_level
| sort - distinct_recipients
queries.sql:
-- SQL for QR Code Payment Fraud (Quishing) Detection
-- Detects emails with QR codes pointing to new domains or credential harvesting pages
SELECT
  e.message_id,
  e.sender_email,
  e.sender_domain,
  e.recipient_email,
  e.subject,
  e.message_timestamp,
  q.qr_destination_url,
  q.qr_destination_fqdn,
  d.domain_age_days AS destination_domain_age,
  q.redirect_final_fqdn,
  rd.domain_age_days AS redirect_final_domain_age,
  CASE
    WHEN d.domain_age_days <= 30 THEN 'new_domain'
    WHEN q.qr_destination_is_shortener = TRUE AND rd.domain_age_days <= 30 THEN 'shortener_to_new_domain'
    WHEN bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE AND bi.is_legitimate = FALSE THEN 'brand_impersonation'
  END AS detection_reason,
  CASE
    WHEN bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE AND d.domain_age_days < 7 THEN 'critical'
    WHEN bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE THEN 'high'
    WHEN q.qr_destination_is_shortener = TRUE AND rd.domain_age_days <= 30 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'medium'
  END AS risk_level
FROM email_messages e
JOIN qr_code_analysis q ON e.message_id = q.message_id
LEFT JOIN domain_intelligence d ON q.qr_destination_fqdn = d.domain_name
LEFT JOIN domain_intelligence rd ON q.redirect_final_fqdn = rd.domain_name
LEFT JOIN brand_impersonation_feed bi ON q.qr_destination_fqdn = bi.domain_name
WHERE q.attachment_contains_qr_code = TRUE
  AND e.message_timestamp >= DATEADD(HOUR, -24, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
  AND (
    d.domain_age_days <= 30
    OR (q.qr_destination_is_shortener = TRUE AND rd.domain_age_days <= 30)
    OR (bi.is_brand_impersonation = TRUE AND bi.is_legitimate = FALSE)
  )
ORDER BY e.message_timestamp DESC

references: INTERPOL, Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment, 2nd Edition (March 2026) — QR Code Scam Targeting Online Sellers
INTERPOL GFFTA 2026 — The Convergence of Impersonation and Identity Fraud
FLAME TP-0050: Calendar/Invite Injection Phishing — comparable off-platform lure delivery
FLAME TP-0037: Digital Wallet / NFC Payment Fraud — mobile money monetization overlap
falsepositives: Legitimate marketing emails containing QR codes linking to new campaign landing pages
Event invitations with QR codes for registration on recently launched event platforms
Payment requests from new merchants using QR-based payment systems
Internal communications using QR codes linking to newly deployed internal tools
